When you acquire this Heroic Skill, choose three different tastes among bitter, salty, sour, sweet, and umami. Then, choose three different effects among the following:

  • You deal 20 (choose one: Dark , Light) damage to each of this delicacy’s targets. Choose the type of this effect when you acquire this Heroic Skill.

Skill Enhancement Lv. 30 ― The damage increases to 30.

  • During the next turn of each of this delicacy’s targets, all damage they deal becomes (choose one: Dark , Light) and its type cannot change. Choose the type of this effect when you acquire this Heroic Skill.
  • For each of this delicacy’s targets, if they are affected by one or more spells with a duration of “Scene”, instead they are no longer affected by any of those spells.
  • Choose yourself or an ally you can see. For each of this delicacy’s targets, the next time that target performs an 【⚔️Attack】 or casts an 【⚡Offensive Spell】 before the end of this scene, that attack or spell must include the chosen creature among its targets (if able).
  • Each of this delicacy’s targets suffers Enraged.
  • Each of this delicacy’s targets suffers Poisoned.
  • Each of this delicacy’s targets recovers 30 Hit Points and 30 Mind Points.

Skill Enhancement Lv. 30 ― The amounts increase to 40 Hit Points and 40 Mind Points.

  • Each of this delicacy’s targets recovers from a single status of their choice.
  • Each of this delicacy’s targets recovers from Dazed, Enraged, and Shaken.
  • Each of this delicacy’s targets recovers from Poisoned, Slow, and Weak.

When you create a delicacy using exactly 3 ingredients during a conflict, if each ingredient matches a different taste among those chosen when you acquired this Heroic Skill, you may ignore all of that delicacy’s normal effects. If you do, you may instead apply one, two, or all of the effects you chose when you acquired this Heroic Skill.

props.classMechanic_text:
GOURMET MECHANIC — COOKING

“A true chef respects the nature of that which they transform.”

What Cooking Does (Beginner-Friendly)

  • Collect Ingredients with tastes: Bitter, Salty, Sour, Sweet, Umami (or sometimes your choice).
  • Spend 1 action to combine 2 or 3 ingredients → you create a Delicacy.

  • Choose one way to deliver it:

    • Serve: Apply the effects to yourself or an ally you can see.
    • Strike: Make a free attack with a weapon you have equipped; the effects are applied to each enemy hit (the attack itself deals no damage unless a Skill says otherwise).
  • Each new pair of tastes you discover gains a permanent, fixed effect in your Cookbook. From then on, that pair always produces that effect.

Ingredient Capacity

You can carry up to 10 + (SL × 5) ingredients. They never spoil until used.

How Many Effects?

A delicacy has 2 effects if it includes 2 tastes; it has 3 effects if you used 3 tastes (see Special Rules).

Cooking — Step-by-Step

  1. Choose 2 or 3 ingredients. Note their tastes (e.g., Bitter + Sweet).
  2. If this taste pair is new to your Cookbook, roll a d12 on the Delicacy Effect table (below). Make any choices the result asks for and record it on your Cookbook. From now on, this pair always produces that exact effect.
  3. Create the delicacy (spend your action). Immediately pick one delivery option: Serve or Strike (free attack).
  4. Apply all effects of the delicacy to every valid target. Then the delicacy is consumed (destroyed).

Knife & Fork synergy (Skill): If you used no more than 2 ingredients and chose the Strike option, the attack may deal its normal damage. Treat your HR (High Roll) as 0 when calculating that damage.

Ingredients & Tastes — Gaining Ingredients (Expanded)

Rest in a Settlement (from Cooking)

Gain [SL] ingredients each time you rest inside a settlement.

Traveling Cook (Skill)

After each travel roll, gain [SL × 2] ingredients.

Rewards During Play

Found as loot, quest rewards, or scene boons at the GM’s discretion.

Buying from Shops/Stalls

  • 10 zenit: 1 ingredient with a random taste.
  • 20 zenit: 1 ingredient with a taste of your choice.

Determining the Taste

Whenever you obtain an ingredient and its taste isn’t specified, roll a d6 and record the result on your cookbook sheet. Then describe its appearance and give it a name.

d6123456
TasteBitterSaltySourSweetUmamiYour choice (pick any taste)

Carry Limit: You can carry 10 + (SL × 5) ingredients. Ingredients never spoil until used.

Starting Stock: If you took Cooking at character creation, begin with 10 ingredients with random tastes.

Changing a Taste (Salt & Pepper): While preparing a delicacy, spend 2 Inventory Points to change the taste of one ingredient to any other taste. (This matters only for the delicacy you’re cooking; the ingredient is consumed.)

Mini-Procedure: Adding Ingredients to Your Sheet

  1. Source? Mark where it came from (Rest / Travel / Reward / Shop 10z / Shop 20z).
  2. Taste? If random, roll d6 using the table above (6 = choose). If 20z, pick a taste directly.
  3. Name & Look: Jot a short name and appearance tag (e.g., “Fossil Honey,” “Stonebark Shroom”).
  4. Update Inventory: Check your carry limit. Ingredients don’t use Inventory Points—your limit is tracked by count.
  5. Cookbook: Only taste pairs belong here. Single ingredients go in your inventory list; pairs & their effects are recorded on the cookbook when discovered.
Examples

Example A — Resting at SL 3: You rest in town and gain 3 ingredients. You roll d6 three times and get 1 (Bitter), 5 (Umami), 6 (Your choice → you pick Sweet). You add “Fossil Honey” (Bitter), “Stonebark Shroom” (Umami), and “Candied Fern” (Sweet) to your inventory.

Example B — Traveling Cook at SL 3: After a travel roll, gain 6 ingredients. Roll six d6, record tastes, and name each. These are great for experimenting with new pairs next scene.

Example C — Buying: You spend 40 z on two chosen-taste ingredients (Sweet and Umami) to chase a combo you’re missing, and 20 z on two random ones (roll twice on the d6 table).

Optional: Quick Stall Stock (GM Helper)

62 chosen-taste slots available (20 z each)

This helper is optional and keeps availability swingy but fair; adjust to taste for your campaign’s economy.

You keep single-ingredient entries in your inventory list.

You record new taste pairs (first time only) on the Cookbook after you roll the d12 effect during Cooking.

Don’t pre-assign effects to ingredients. Only pairs get effects, and only when discovered via Cooking.

Salt & Pepper doesn’t permanently change stored items—it just changes one ingredient’s taste as you cook (and that item is consumed).

Delicacy Effect Table (d12) — simplified text

Each newly discovered pair of tastes gets one of these results permanently in your Cookbook. Effects marked with numbers 5–12 only apply during conflict scenes.

d12Combination Effect
1Each target recovers from one status (choose: Dazed, Enraged, Poisoned, Shaken, Slow, Weak).
2Each target suffers one status (choose: Dazed, Shaken, Slow, Weak).
3Each target recovers 40 HP (50 if you are level 30+).
4Each target recovers 40 MP (50 if you are level 30+).
5Deal 20 (30 if level 30+) damage of one type to each target: Air, Bolt, Earth, Fire, Ice, Poison.
6Until the end of your next turn, sources that deal the chosen damage type ( Air/Bolt/Earth/Fire/Ice/Poison) deal +5 extra damage to each target.
7Targets cannot perform Guard during their next turn.
8Targets cannot perform a Spell during their next turn.
9Targets cannot perform a Skill during their next turn.
10Targets gain Resistance to one damage type until end of your next turn (choose: Air, Bolt, Earth, Fire, Ice, Poison).
11Each target treats one Attribute as one die size higher (max d12) until the end of your next turn: Dexterity, Insight, Might, or Willpower.
12During their next turn, all damage each target deals becomes one chosen type and its type cannot change: Air/Bolt/Earth/Fire/Ice/Poison.

Special Rules (Keep It Straight)

  • Different tastes = more effects. Each distinct pair of tastes (even using the same taste twice, e.g., Sweet + Sweet) adds an effect.
  • New pair? Roll d12 & record it. No two Cookbook pairs can have identical effects. If a new roll would duplicate an existing effect, make choices to avoid it; if still impossible, reroll.
  • 2 tastes → 2 effects. 3 tastes → 3 effects.
  • Only one type-5 effect (damage-dealing) per delicacy. If multiple results would add type-5, choose one and ignore the rest.
  • Only one type-12 effect (damage-type change) per delicacy. If you’d get more than one, choose one and ignore the others.
  • Effects 5–12 can only be applied during conflict scenes.
  • When complete, your Cookbook will list 15 total effects (one for each possible pair of tastes).
  • Delicacies take effect immediately and are then destroyed. To store food with unique effects and use later, craft them as Projects.

Free Benefits & Helpful Synergies

  • +2 Inventory Points (permanent).
  • Projects to create unique foods & drinks; always consumable and sized for the number of targets you need to feed.
  • Traveling Cook (Skill): After each travel roll, gain (SL × 2) ingredients.
  • Made With Love (Skill): When you Serve a delicacy to yourself or an ally, you may spend up to (SL × 10) MP. For every 10 MP spent, apply the delicacy to one additional ally you can see.

Quick Cooking Card (hand to players)

  1. Pick 2–3 ingredients you carry.
  2. New pair? Roll d12 on the Delicacy table and write it in your Cookbook.
  3. Cook (1 action) → choose Serve (ally buff / heal) or Strike (free attack; effects on enemies).
  4. Apply all effects to each target. Delicacy is consumed.
  5. Knife & Fork: If 2 ingredients, your free attack may deal damage (HR counts as 0).

Play Tips

  • Scout outside combat. You may prepare delicacies out of conflict to learn & record effects without pressure.
  • Synergy watch: Healing (3–4) + Resist (10) + Attribute boost (11) can set up a safe push; Damage (5–6) pairs great with disabling (7–9).
  • Share the love: Use Made With Love MP to spread big buffs to the whole team.
